Questions 19 to 26
You are going to read an extract from an article, for questions 19- 26, choose the correct answer (A,
B, Cor D) and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet.
As the taxi pulled to a stop, Hamdan hastily stowed his luggage in the trunk and he
exchanged a quick greeting with the driver. As he watched the familiar scene outside the window,
he felt nervous about the trip home. The digital hum of his phone provided lttle solace. Opening
emails, he revisited the ominous message from his employer - the layoff letter, a harsh
consequence of the company's dwindling fortunes. Fortwo months, he had scoured the job market
to no avail. He had no alternative but to leave the city because he could no longer afford the rent
and the car monthly installment.
Lost in thought, the abrupt halt of the taxi jolted him back to the reality. He looked out to
find himself at his destination, the two-hour drive felt like a blur. As the taxi drove off into the
distance, he stood before a timber house-a childhood home he had not visited in over four years
The house still stands grandly on the stilts with its welcoming green stairs. Dragging his luggage
along the unpaved road, memories surged. His mother emerged with a smile on her face. She
came down the green stairs and Hamdan shook her hand and apologised for being gone for so
long. His father, appearing from beneath the house, greeted him with a farmer's tool in hand. The
handshake carried an unspoken tension, a silent battle fought and unresolved.
His mother told Hamdan that she had cleaned his room. Swinging open the door, Hamdan
was met with the nostalgia of his bedroom, frozen in time. A new addition, an air conditioner,
showed his parents' efforts to provide him the comfort he long yearned for. Afterwards, Hamdan
wandered around the house like a lost strange in his own home. New furniture in the house showed
that life had moved on. He entered the kitchen and then proceeded to the bathroom for a refreshing
shower. The newly renovated bathroom left him in awe, considering he used to rely on an outdoor
bathroom and toilet. Now, his parents had expanded the kitchen and constructed a new bathroom
and toilet, connected to the kitchen.
When his mother saw how amazed he was, she smiled and asked if he liked the house. Hamdan
nodded and asked when they had started making these changes. She told him that the toilet had
been built with the money Hamdan had sent every month. They had carefully saved money and
decided to build the bathroom because his father was getting old and had knee problems that
made going outside difficult. Hamdan nodded to show that he understood as he looked at his
father's hair, which now had many more silver strands than it did when Hamdan left home years
ago.

In the evening, he took his father's motorcycle and rode through the village to see the
changes. He pulled over at a coffee stall. He and his friends used to hang out there after school.
While sipping the coffee, he was greeted by his old crush, Aisyah. Hamdan learnt that she
returned to the village a month ago to care for her parents. He was even happier when he found
out she wasn't married yet. They spent half an hour catching up with each other. The motorcycle
journey continued to his father's farm, where he saw the workers toiled. Seeking his father among
the goats, Hamdan offered to help, a request met with surprise. Assigned the task of mucking the
cow's barn, he embraced the labour, a reminder of simpler times.
Thoughts filled his mind as he rode home. The sight of his aging father and a chance
encounter with an old flame left Hamdan pondering. He spent his younger years dreaming of city
life, but it didn't bring the happiness he expected. The next morning, he informed his parents of
his wish to help the farm. His father, remembering past arguments, asked if he was sure about
staying in the village. Hamdan, understanding his dad's worry, said maybe a change in his life
might bring him peace. Seeing the shared glanced between his parents, he sensed a silent
acceptance. Hamdan felt at home and anticipated his future in the village as he began his fresh
start.
(Adapted from Pelangi Skor A+ 2024)

Ways to Spot and Avoid Scams
For any avid movie streamers, receiving Netflix emails about what to watch is common. Hence, a new
message prompting to update account information may look common - especially when it begins with the
familiar red Netflix logo on top. However, the urgency that the message carries - "Please update your
subscription details, or your membership will suspended within 48 hours. "- should be good enough red flag to
notify users that it is indeed a phishing scam attempt. 27
Such common phishing emails and even WhatsApp messages these days, are engineered to trick
recipients into providing credit card and debit card numbers, bank details or even Netflix password. 28
Yet, not all users are cautious enough to avoid befalling into these criminal hands. Without much caution, the
banking account information is keyed into false website will go to fraudsters, allowing legal money withdrawals
and transactions.
It is utmost important to always be wary as no respectable company or government department will
simply demand you toconfirm your identity by filling out forms, often accessible by clicking an attached
hyperlink. Phishing usually redirects users to a phony website to input information, and often look almost
identical to official websites of impersonated companies. 29 ] Sometimes, they will give a much more
alarming notification like someone is trying to access your account or notify you about a huge sum of unknown
transaction.
In addition, what is currently trending today is 'vishing' or 'voice phishing . 30 Some would
prompt the victims tomake certain transactions in order to solve whatever problems they are accused of doing
Sometimes, victims are asked to follow a set of instructions online on their computers, before the computers
are taken control by these evil scammers. Either way, victims usually are cheated a significant amount of
money.
Surprisingly, seniors are not the only ones that fall victims to scammers. Despite being born in high-
tech world, members of Generation Z (born in the late 1990s and early 2000s) are also falling for vishing and
online scams. 31. Some even fell for tricky advertisements that said they were entitled for certain
government financial aid or free cosmetic products.

Notwithstanding, you do not really need to unplug and return to pre-digital age to save yourself. Setting strong password can prevent becoming scam victims. (32) ____________. Besides, double your effort by opting for two-factor authentication for banking-related apps. Having a one-time code sent to your mobile devices can really help ensure account security.

A You may now be locked out of your accounts because the scammers have access to your accounts.

B When this comes via text message, it is called “smishing” or “SMS phishing”.

C If meticulously observed, the login interface will look slightly different than the legitimate ones.

D In fact, a cybersecurity firm observed an increment of 156 percent victims aged 20 and younger between 2017 and 2020.

E For example, you can choose ones with at least seven characters with combined uppercase and lowercase letters.

F Thus, you should be wary of the words used in the emails and take time to scrutinise the content.

G Whenever in doubt, contact the company or organisation to confirm if it is really them.

H To illustrate this, every day, a huge number of victims receive phone calls from tax department, banks and even police stations, which can be convincing and threatening.

Popular Online Shopping Platforms in Malaysia
A- LAZADA
One of the largest and most popular e-commerce platforms in Malaysia, Lazada offers a wide
range of products from electronics to fashion There are three different types of sellers on Lazada.
LazMall sellers are official brands or authorised sellers, local sellers which are based in Malaysia
and LazGlobal sellers which are based in China, Korea or Japan. If you don't feel comfortable
buying from sellers you aren't familiar with, you can just stick to buying from official brands.
B- SHOPEE
A major competitor to Lazada, Shopee is known for its user-friendly interface and frequent
promotions. Shopee has rapidly become one of the top choices for online shopping in Malaysia.
Shoppe is favourited by most teenagers as it has user-friendly interface, extensive range of
products, competitive pricing, and innovative features like Shopee Coins, various vouchers for
upcoming buys, and daily flash sales. Its mobile-first approach appeals to the tech-savvy younger
generation.
C- MUDAH.MY
Malaysia's largest marketplace for buying and selling second-hand items and it offers wide range
of categories from vehicles to real estate, user-friendly platform, and the ability to find good deals
on used items. However, buyers are not protected because there is no rating system to record
successful purchases thus opting for cash on delivery (COD) is the best assurance you can get
before making payment.
D- CAROUSELL
A classifieds marketplace where users can buy and sell new and used items, ranging from
fashion to electronics. Health and beauty products tend to be popular. Unlike Mudah.my, this

platform enforces a rating system to ensure buyers get a secured purchasing experience
Besides, it has its own payment system, on which money will be withheld until buyers check they
items they get. Buyers also have the ability to negotiate prices directly with sellers.
E-ZALORA
Zalora is a leading online fashion and lifestyle platform in Malaysia. Unlike local online shopping
platforms, Zalora provides exclusive deals on international and local fashion brands, easy return
policies, and curated collections. They cater to fashion enthusiasts looking for trendy and high-
quality apparel. While prices are sometimes more expensive than local retailers, during sales,
buyers can save up to 70% on old stocks. Despite discounts, any items you purchase are
definitely genuine.
F- E-BAY
While not as dominant as local platforms, it remains popular for niche products and international
purchases. It also has accessed to international sellers, availability of rare and unique items, and
a trusted platform for global transactions. However, be ready to pay hefty shipping fees as most
sellers are based in western countries and some even reluctant to ship to Malaysia.
